model.name: Occurrence / Event
model.purpose: Generic events: what happened, when, where, who, on what evidence, and how one happening relates to another, without assuming an intentional actor.
model.scope_statement: Format-neutral world-model for a discrete happening in cultural, social, physical or computational systems. It records the occurrence itself, its temporal and spatial extent, participants and present objects, causal and meronymic links, source accounts, certainty, and the lifecycle of the record that stands for the happening. Specialized models such as Act and Encounter extend this backbone rather than reinventing time, place, participation and causality.
in_scope: A particular that unfolded or is unfolding in time (CIDOC E5 Event / BFO occurrent-process analogue)
Identity and type of the happening
Actors and objects present and the roles they played
Asserted cause, influence and part-whole structure
Distinction between world-event time and record observation or ingestion time
Record status including amendment, corroboration, invalidation and entered-in-error
Stewardship, access, retention and alignment to external event vocabularies
Both agentive activities and non-agentive happenings such as earthquakes
Independence from JSON, YAML, HTML, Git, MCP or MongoDB projections
out_of_scope: Intentional or causal-actor specialization of a happening belongs in WM-ACT-002 Act (CIDOC E7 Activity / PROV Activity with an associated Agent).
Reciprocal participation and mutual encounter semantics belong in WM-ACT-018 Encounter.
Persistent persons, organizations, devices and other continuants are referenced, not mastered here.
Canonical addresses, geocodes, POIs and location referents belong in a location/address sibling.
Recurring phenomenon types and event classes as scientific kinds belong in an observed-phenomenon sibling; this model holds the particular instantiation.
Standing situations and conditions (CIDOC E3 Condition State; FHIR Condition) belong in a situation sibling that occurrences may open, advance or close.
Audit of record-keeping operations belongs in an audit-trail sibling.
Access-grant contracts belong in an access-control sibling; this model only records which participation is disclosable.
Supply-chain traces compose occurrences; the trace itself belongs in WM-FLW-013.

Plans, orders and requests (FHIR Request pattern; PROV Plan; schema.org Schedule) are not occurrences until or unless they are performed. Cancelled or postponed scheduled public events remain plans until a world happening occurs.
Software routing envelopes, protocol bindings and payload codecs (CloudEvents message/protocol) are interchange projections, not the world occurrence.
Legal instruments, contracts and rights are not events; a signing or breach may be recorded as an occurrence referencing those instruments.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Event record (CloudEvents Event, FHIR recorded, EPCIS recordTime)
boundary_notes.distinction: The occurrence is the world happening; the event record is a statement about it. CloudEvents explicitly separates Occurrence from Event (data record). FHIR separates occurrence[x] from recorded. EPCIS separates eventTime from recordTime. This model must keep that cut.
CIDOC E5 Event is a change-bearing process with spatiotemporal extent; schema.org Event is typically a scheduled public happening that can be cancelled before it occurs. Alignment is not identity.

boundary_notes.neighbor: BFO occurrent hierarchy (Process and process boundary)
boundary_notes.distinction: BFO ISO/IEC 21838-2 has no separate Event class: occurrents that unfold are processes; instantaneous beginnings and endings are process boundaries. Instantaneous overall effect is a coarse description, not a distinct ontological kind.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Act / agentive specialization and FHIR Event.subject
boundary_notes.distinction: An occurrence may have zero agents (a flood). Adding a required performer or subject is a specialization (FHIR Event.subject is 1..1 in the clinical pattern and must not be imposed here).

boundary_notes.neighbor: Location / address sibling and virtual attendance modes
boundary_notes.distinction: Place is a specification that resolves through a location sibling. VirtualLocation and OnlineEventAttendanceMode are attendance modes, not substitutes for a location master.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Physical causal law versus asserted influence
boundary_notes.distinction: Causality is asserted, qualified and evidential (PROV Influence; CIDOC P15 was influenced by), not a closed physical law.
Conformance to CIDOC CRM, schema.org, EPCIS, PROV, FHIR or CloudEvents is an alignment claim that must be evidenced per instance, never assumed by storing this model.

bundles.name: Happening
bundles.description: Identify the occurrence as a world particular, classify it, and locate it in time and space without requiring an agent.
bundles.rationale: Identity, kind, time and place are the minimum a happening needs before any participant or explanation is asserted, so grouping them keeps the agentless case valid on its own.

layers.name: Occurrence core
layers.description: Identity, kind, narrative and the occurrence-versus-record cut.

findings.name: Occurrence identity
findings.description: An occurrence is a distinct delimited coherent process or interaction that happens over a contiguous temporal extent and cannot happen twice as the same particular. Identity is carried by a registrar or producer identifier, optionally a governed IRI, and only then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. CloudEvents requires source plus id uniqueness for each distinct event record of an occurrence; CIDOC identifies CRM entities by appellation and preferred identifier (P1, P48/E42). A calendar date is not an identifier.

questions.text: What authoritative master-system identifier uniquely denotes this occurrence within the producing registrar, and which system assigned it?
Does a governed global identifier or IRI exist for this occurrence, and how does it relate to the master-system identifier?
Which producer source scope plus identifier pair is treated as duplicate, and may a later retransmission reuse that pair?
Which appellations, including dates or calendar labels, are names rather than identifiers and must not be used as the occurrence primary key?

data_elements.name: master_system_id
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier assigned to the occurrence by the producing registrar or master system.

data_elements.name: master_system_uri
data_elements.description: URI form of the master-system identifier where the assigning system publishes one.

data_elements.name: global_iri
data_elements.description: Governed global IRI for the occurrence where one exists.

data_elements.name: dimension_uuid
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only after master-system and governed identifiers are absent.

data_elements.name: cloud_source
data_elements.description: CloudEvents source context attribute whose combination with the event id must be unique for each distinct event record.

data_elements.name: preferred_appellation
data_elements.description: Preferred name of the occurrence (CIDOC P1, P48/E42), used as a label and never as the primary key.

data_elements.name: same_as
data_elements.description: Equivalent identifiers or IRIs asserted to denote the same occurrence particular.

artifacts.name: Occurrence record
artifacts.description: Canonical occurrence identity document holding master identifier, optional IRI and appellations, independent of storage format.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier first, then governed global IRI, then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; dates and appellations are names, not keys.

findings.name: Kind and classification
findings.description: Occurrences are typed. CIDOC P2 has type / E55 Type (examples: wedding, earthquake, skirmish) and E5 versus E7 Activity distinguish non-agentive happenings from activities. Schema.org Event uses additionalType, keywords and a public-event subtype tree; CloudEvents type is a reverse-DNS routing class of the originating occurrence; EPCIS separates technical event type (ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent, AssociationEvent) from business step (bizStep) and disposition. FHIR Event has category and code for the service performed. No single typology is universal; the model stores a primary kind plus alignment codes.

questions.text: What is the primary kind of this happening, in which scheme, and is it an agentive activity or a non-agentive process?
If used in a visibility or custody setting, what technical event type, business step and disposition apply?
Which additional types from schema.org, CIDOC, FHIR or a reverse-DNS CloudEvents type should be recorded for routing and search without claiming full conformance?

data_elements.name: primary_kind
data_elements.description: Primary kind of the happening in the declared classification scheme.

data_elements.name: kind_scheme
data_elements.description: URI of the vocabulary in which the primary kind is defined.

data_elements.name: is_activity
data_elements.description: Whether the happening is an agentive activity (CIDOC E7) rather than a non-agentive event (E5).

data_elements.name: epcis_event_type
data_elements.description: EPCIS technical event type such as ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent or AssociationEvent.

data_elements.name: business_step
data_elements.description: EPCIS business step (bizStep) describing the business context of the happening.

data_elements.name: additional_types
data_elements.description: Additional type codes from schema.org, CIDOC, FHIR or a reverse-DNS CloudEvents type, recorded for routing and search.

data_elements.name: keywords
data_elements.description: Free keywords attached to the occurrence for search, as in schema.org Event keywords.

artifacts.name: Occurrence kind assignment
artifacts.description: Typed classification of an occurrence against one or more vocabularies, with scheme URIs and activity-versus-happening flag.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus primary kind code and scheme URI.

findings.name: Summary and aboutness
findings.description: An occurrence has a human-readable name or summary and may be about other entities. Schema.org Event requires name and allows description, disambiguatingDescription, about and workFeatured or workPerformed. CIDOC P3 has note and P129 is about. FHIR Event.note captures comments by performer or subject. The summary is not a substitute for structured type, time or participants.

questions.text: What short summary distinguishes this occurrence from similar happenings, and in which language?
Which entities, works or topics is the occurrence about or did it feature, without treating those as participants?
What disambiguating description is required when name and type are insufficient to separate this particular from another of the same kind?

data_elements.name: name
data_elements.description: Human-readable name of the occurrence, as required by schema.org Event.

data_elements.name: summary
data_elements.description: Short summary that distinguishes this occurrence from similar happenings.

data_elements.name: description
data_elements.description: Longer description or note about the happening (schema.org description; CIDOC P3 has note; FHIR Event.note).

data_elements.name: about_refs
data_elements.description: Entities, works or topics the occurrence is about (CIDOC P129 is about; schema.org about, workFeatured, workPerformed), which are not participants.

data_elements.name: language
data_elements.description: BCP 47 language tag of the name, summary and description text.

artifacts.name: Occurrence narrative
artifacts.description: Language-tagged name, summary and optional notes used to disambiguate the happening.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus BCP 47 language tag.

layers.name: Temporality
layers.description: Instants, intervals, fuzzy bounds, temporal reference systems, ordering and the split between event time and record time.

findings.name: Temporal extent
findings.description: Every occurrence occupies a temporal entity: an instant, a proper interval, or a fuzzy time-span. OWL-Time models TemporalEntity as Instant or Interval, Allen interval relations, duration and hasBeginning/hasEnd. CIDOC E2 Temporal Entity has P4 has time-span to E52 Time-Span with inner bound P81 ongoing throughout and outer bound P82 at some time within, plus P79/P80 qualitative begin/end and P191 duration. FHIR occurrence[x] is dateTime, Period or Timing. RFC 3339 covers only instants with explicit UTC offset, not intervals or non-Gregorian calendars. CIDOC states the same event cannot happen twice; a later recurrence is a new occurrence.

questions.text: Is the happening an instant, a proper interval, an ongoing interval, or only a fuzzy outer bound, and what are the begin and end if known?
What inner (ongoing throughout) and outer (at some time within) bounds, and which begin/end qualifications, express uncertainty of the phenomenal time-span?
What duration is asserted, in which unit or ISO 8601 duration literal, and is it derived from bounds or independently observed?
Which Allen or CIDOC temporal primitives relate this occurrence to other temporal entities (meets, overlaps, during, starts-before, ends-before)?

data_elements.name: temporal_shape
data_elements.description: Whether the occurrence is an instant, a proper interval, an ongoing interval or only a fuzzy outer bound.

data_elements.name: begin_instant
data_elements.description: Beginning of the temporal extent as an RFC 3339 instant where known.

data_elements.name: end_instant
data_elements.description: End of the temporal extent as an RFC 3339 instant where known.

data_elements.name: inner_bound
data_elements.description: Inner bound of the time-span during which the occurrence was ongoing throughout (CIDOC P81).

data_elements.name: outer_bound
data_elements.description: Outer bound within which the occurrence happened at some time (CIDOC P82).

data_elements.name: duration
data_elements.description: Duration of the occurrence as an ISO 8601 duration literal (CIDOC P191; OWL-Time duration).

data_elements.name: ongoing
data_elements.description: Whether the occurrence is still unfolding and therefore has no asserted end.

data_elements.name: allen_relations
data_elements.description: Allen interval or CIDOC temporal relations linking this occurrence to other temporal entities.

artifacts.name: Time specification
artifacts.description: Structured temporal extent for an occurrence: shape, bounds, duration, TRS and qualitative qualifications.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier; the temporal position itself is never used as the occurrence key.

findings.name: Event time versus observation time
findings.description: Event time (when the occurrence happened) must be recorded separately from observation, ingestion or record time (when a source captured or a registrar ingested the statement) whenever they differ. EPCIS requires eventTime, optional recordTime and eventTimeZoneOffset. FHIR has occurrence[x] versus recorded. CloudEvents time is timestamp of when the occurrence happened, but producers MAY fall back to another time if occurrence time cannot be determined, provided all producers for a source are consistent. RFC 3339 timestamps for Internet instants MUST include seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; unqualified local time is not interoperable; unknown local offset may use -00:00. Leap seconds may appear as second=60.

questions.text: When did the occurrence happen, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and explicit offset or Z, or why is event time unknown?
When was the occurrence first observed or the record ingested, and which clock or producer algorithm supplied that instant?
Is the recorded time the actual occurrence time, a consistent producer fallback, or an unknown-offset local time using the RFC 3339 -00:00 convention?

data_elements.name: event_time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the occurrence happened, with seconds and explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: event_time_zone_offset
data_elements.description: Local UTC offset in force where the occurrence happened, as EPCIS eventTimeZoneOffset.

data_elements.name: observation_time
data_elements.description: Instant at which a source first observed or captured the happening.

data_elements.name: ingestion_time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the registrar ingested the record, corresponding to EPCIS recordTime and FHIR recorded.

data_elements.name: time_basis
data_elements.description: Whether the stored time is the actual occurrence time, a consistent producer fallback, or an unknown-offset local time.

data_elements.name: unknown_offset_flag
data_elements.description: Whether the RFC 3339 -00:00 unknown-local-offset convention was used.

artifacts.name: Dual timestamp block
artifacts.description: Paired event-time and observation/ingestion-time values with offset, basis and unknown-offset convention.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus time basis, keeping event time and observation or ingestion time distinguishable.

findings.name: Temporal reference system and precision
findings.description: OWL-Time requires a TRS on TemporalPosition and supports Gregorian DateTimeDescription, numeric coordinates (Unix, Julian day, GPS) and ordinal systems (geologic, dynastic). Precision is the unitType of the datetime description. Historical and archaeological occurrences often cannot use RFC 3339 Gregorian instants. ISO 19108 calendars, clocks and ordinal scales are aligned, not owned.

questions.text: Which temporal reference system, calendar or ordinal scale positions this occurrence?
What is the coarsest temporal unit that the position actually supports (year, day, second, geologic stage)?
If Gregorian RFC 3339 is inapplicable, what numeric or nominal position is used and how is it mapped for ordering?

data_elements.name: trs_uri
data_elements.description: URI of the temporal reference system against which the occurrence position is expressed.

data_elements.name: precision_unit
data_elements.description: Coarsest temporal unit the position actually supports, as the unitType of the datetime description.

data_elements.name: calendar_system
data_elements.description: Calendar or ordinal scale used, where it is not the Gregorian calendar.

data_elements.name: numeric_position
data_elements.description: Numeric temporal coordinate such as Unix time, Julian day or GPS time.

data_elements.name: nominal_position
data_elements.description: Ordinal or nominal temporal position such as a geologic stage or dynastic period.

artifacts.name: TRS binding
artifacts.description: Declared temporal reference system, calendar and precision for the occurrence's temporal position.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus TRS URI.

layers.name: Spatiality
layers.description: Where the happening took place, at stated granularity, including virtual attendance without owning the location master.

findings.name: Place, granularity and attendance mode
findings.description: CIDOC E5/E4 took place at E53 Place (P7) or on or within an E18 Physical Thing (P8); Place is a physical extent independent of matter, often relative to a frame of reference (P157), not only WGS84. Schema.org location may be Place, PostalAddress, Text or VirtualLocation; eventAttendanceMode is Offline, Online or Mixed, with separate maximumAttendeeCapacity, maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity and maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity. EPCIS splits readPoint (where the observation was made) from bizLocation (where the object is believed to be). PROV atLocation applies to Activity, Entity, Agent or InstantaneousEvent. FHIR Event.location is the principal physical location. Place specifications here REFERENCE a location sibling.

questions.text: Where did the occurrence take place, at what granularity, and which location-sibling identifier or relative frame is used?
Was attendance offline, online or mixed, and what virtual location URI applies if any?
For observed object events, what is the read point versus the business location, and may they differ?
If place is unknown, unknowable or classified, what placeholder and disclosure constraint apply?

data_elements.name: place_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the location sibling record for where the occurrence took place.

data_elements.name: place_granularity
data_elements.description: Granularity at which the place is asserted, from precise extent to coarse region.

data_elements.name: frame_of_reference_ref
data_elements.description: Frame of reference relative to which the place extent is defined (CIDOC P157), where it is not an absolute geocode.

data_elements.name: attendance_mode
data_elements.description: Offline, online or mixed attendance mode of the happening.

data_elements.name: virtual_location
data_elements.description: URI of the virtual locus where online attendance took place.

data_elements.name: read_point_ref
data_elements.description: EPCIS read point where the observation of the objects was made.

data_elements.name: business_location_ref
data_elements.description: EPCIS business location where the object is believed to be after the event.

data_elements.name: unknown_place
data_elements.description: Whether place is unknown, unknowable or withheld, triggering the placeholder and disclosure rule.

artifacts.name: Place specification
artifacts.description: Where-it-happened statement: location reference, granularity, attendance mode, read-point versus business location.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus the referenced location-sibling identifier or relative frame of reference.

bundles.name: Involvement
bundles.description: Who or what took part or was merely present, and in what capacity, without requiring an intentional actor.
bundles.rationale: Participation, presence and role qualification share the subject-optional constraint, so they are grouped apart from the happening itself to keep agentless occurrences valid.

layers.name: Participants and presence
layers.description: Actors, objects present, used entities and the optional subject of a clinical-style event.

findings.name: Participants, presence and used objects
findings.description: CIDOC P11 had participant links E5 Event to E39 Actor; the broader P12 occurred in the presence of links to any E77 Persistent Item. E7 Activity adds P14 carried out by with P14.1 in the role of, P16 used specific object, and P125 used object of type. Schema.org distinguishes organizer, performer, attendee, contributor, sponsor and composer. PROV associates Agents with Activities (wasAssociatedWith) and records used/generated Entities. FHIR Event requires a subject the action was performed on/for, plus optional performer.actor; that 1..1 subject must not be imposed on generic world events. EPCIS ObjectEvent lists EPCs or quantities the event happened to; AggregationEvent adds parent/child; TransformationEvent records inputs and outputs. Presence is not the same as participation or performance.

questions.text: Which actors participated, which persistent items were merely present, and which objects were used or generated?
Is there a subject on or for whom the happening was performed, and is that subject distinct from the performer?
Is this a non-agentive happening with no participant, and what evidence still documents it?
For visibility events, which instance or class-level object identifiers, parent-child aggregations or transformation inputs and outputs are in scope?

data_elements.name: participant_refs
data_elements.description: Actors that participated in the occurrence (CIDOC P11 had participant).

data_elements.name: present_item_refs
data_elements.description: Persistent items that were present without participating (CIDOC P12 occurred in the presence of).

data_elements.name: used_object_refs
data_elements.description: Objects used in the happening (CIDOC P16 used specific object; PROV used).

data_elements.name: generated_entity_refs
data_elements.description: Entities generated by the happening (PROV wasGeneratedBy; EPCIS transformation outputs).

data_elements.name: subject_ref
data_elements.description: Optional subject on or for whom the happening was performed; never required on the generic occurrence.

data_elements.name: epc_list
data_elements.description: Instance or class-level object identifiers the visibility event happened to.

data_elements.name: has_no_agent
data_elements.description: Whether this is a non-agentive happening with no participant or performer.

artifacts.name: Participation set
artifacts.description: Set of participation and presence statements for an occurrence, including used and generated objects.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier; members are references to person, organization or object siblings.

layers.name: Roles
layers.description: The capacity in which each involved party or object figured.

findings.name: Role qualification
findings.description: Role is a qualified relation, not a type of person. CIDOC P14.1 in the role of types how an actor carried out an activity. PROV qualified Association uses hadRole / Role and hadPlan. FHIR performer.function distinguishes type of involvement. Schema.org uses distinct properties (organizer, performer, attendee) rather than a generic role qualifier. Delegation (PROV actedOnBehalfOf) records that one agent acted for another. Presence versus participation versus performance must remain distinct.

questions.text: In what role did each party act, from which scheme, and is that role organizer, performer, attendee, witness, registrar or another capacity?
Did the party act on behalf of another agent, under which plan or mandate?
Was the party physically present, virtually present, represented, or only associated after the fact?

data_elements.name: party_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the party or object whose involvement is being qualified.

data_elements.name: role_code
data_elements.description: Role in which the party figured in the occurrence (CIDOC P14.1; PROV hadRole; FHIR performer.function).

data_elements.name: role_scheme
data_elements.description: URI of the vocabulary from which the role code is taken.

data_elements.name: presence_mode
data_elements.description: Whether the party was physically present, virtually present, represented, or only associated after the fact.

data_elements.name: on_behalf_of_ref
data_elements.description: Agent on whose behalf the party acted (PROV actedOnBehalfOf).

data_elements.name: plan_ref
data_elements.description: Plan or mandate under which the party acted (PROV hadPlan).

artifacts.name: Participation role assignment
artifacts.description: Qualified involvement of one party or object in an occurrence, including role, presence mode and delegation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus party reference plus role code and role scheme.

bundles.name: Explanation
bundles.description: How happenings cause, influence, inform, continue or compose one another.
bundles.rationale: Influence links and part-whole episodes are both asserted knowledge claims about how happenings relate, so they are governed together with asserter, confidence and evidence.

layers.name: Causality and influence
layers.description: Asserted cause, contribution, communication and derivation between occurrences and entities.

findings.name: Causal and influence links
findings.description: CIDOC P15 was influenced by, P17 was motivated by, P20/P21 purpose, and P134 continued relate activities; they are not a closed causal calculus. PROV wasInformedBy (activity-activity communication), wasDerivedFrom (entity-entity), wasGeneratedBy/used, wasInfluencedBy as superproperty, and qualified Influence with optional role and time. Confidence and asserter are required because influence is a knowledge claim. TransformationEvent in EPCIS records identity-changing processes (CIDOC E81 analogue). Do not treat correlation or Allen overlap as causation.

questions.text: What kind of link is asserted (caused, contributed, influenced, motivated, continued, informed, derived, generated, used, transformed) and between which ends?
Who asserted the link, when, at what confidence, and on which source accounts?
Is the link causal or merely temporal overlap or co-location, and which test forbids treating overlap as cause?
Did the happening destroy, produce or transform persistent identities, and which input and output identities result?

data_elements.name: link_kind
data_elements.description: Kind of asserted link: caused, contributed, influenced, motivated, continued, informed, derived, generated, used or transformed.

data_elements.name: from_ref
data_elements.description: Origin end of the directed influence link.

data_elements.name: to_ref
data_elements.description: Target end of the directed influence link.

data_elements.name: confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence attached to the influence claim.

data_elements.name: asserted_by_ref
data_elements.description: Agent that asserted the influence link, required because influence is a knowledge claim.

data_elements.name: asserted_at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the link was asserted.

data_elements.name: qualification
data_elements.description: Qualified influence detail such as role and time, following the PROV qualified pattern.

artifacts.name: Causal or influence link
artifacts.description: Directed qualified link between occurrences or entities stating influence kind, confidence and asserter.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the from and to references plus link kind and asserter; links are append-only claims.

layers.name: Aggregation and episodes
layers.description: Part-whole composition of occurrences, series and fulfillment of plans.

findings.name: Episodes, sub-events and fulfillment
findings.description: CIDOC P9 consists of / P5 consists of compose periods and events; a birth can be both a single E5 Event and an E4 Period of component processes. Schema.org subEvent/superEvent and EventSeries group public happenings; eventSchedule associates a repeating Schedule and forbids startDate/endDate on that Event. FHIR partOf nests an event in a larger event; basedOn links to the Request or Definition fulfilled. EPCIS AggregationEvent records physical pack/unpack. An episode is a narrative composite with its own span, not a new ontological primitive beyond meronymy. Recurrence produces new occurrence particulars.

questions.text: Which member occurrences compose this episode, and which parent does this occurrence form part of?
Is this a series, a scheduled recurrence template, or a single instance, and are instance start and end forbidden because a Schedule carries them?
Which plan, order or request does this occurrence fulfill in whole or in part?
If objects were packed or unpacked, what parent identifier, children and ADD/DELETE/OBSERVE action apply?

data_elements.name: parent_occurrence_ref
data_elements.description: Parent occurrence or period of which this happening forms part (CIDOC P9; FHIR partOf; schema.org superEvent).

data_elements.name: member_occurrence_refs
data_elements.description: Member occurrences composing this episode or super-event (schema.org subEvent).

data_elements.name: episode_kind
data_elements.description: Kind of composite: narrative episode, period, series instance or physical aggregation.

data_elements.name: based_on_request_ref
data_elements.description: Plan, order or request that this occurrence fulfills (FHIR basedOn; PROV Plan).

data_elements.name: series_ref
data_elements.description: EventSeries or recurrence template of which this occurrence is an instance.

data_elements.name: member_count
data_elements.description: Count of member occurrences in the composite, recomputed after membership changes.

artifacts.name: Episode or composite occurrence
artifacts.description: Composite occurrence grouping member happenings, optional series membership and fulfillment of a request or plan.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified as an occurrence in its own right under the occurrence identity priority; membership links carry the member identifiers.

bundles.name: Evidence and record
bundles.description: Source accounts, certainty, dispute, and the lifecycle of the record that stands for the happening.
bundles.rationale: Source accounts and record lifecycle both concern the record that stands for the happening rather than the happening itself, and must stay on the record side of the occurrence-versus-record cut.

layers.name: Sources and certainty
layers.description: Who reported the happening, from which primary source, at what reliability, and whether accounts corroborate or conflict.

findings.name: Source accounts, primary source and certainty
findings.description: PROV hadPrimarySource cites an entity produced by an agent with direct experience; wasQuotedFrom and wasRevisionOf further qualify derivation; Attribution assigns responsibility for an entity. FHIR reported[x] flags a secondary report versus a primary source-of-truth record, with reportedReference to the reporter. CIDOC requires some evidence (witnesses, traces or products) for an event to be documented even if effects were not permanent. Multiple independent accounts may report the same happening; certainty is a function of corroboration, not of a single stored flag. CloudEvents warns that context attributes are inspectable in the clear and must not carry sensitive payload.

questions.text: Who reported this account, when, and is it a primary source-of-truth record or a secondary report?
What reliability and certainty are assigned to this account, and which independent accounts corroborate or contradict it?
Which sensor reading, witness statement, product, trace or document is the primary source entity, and was the narrative quoted or revised from it?
Which facts must remain in encrypted or restricted event data rather than inspectable context attributes?

data_elements.name: source_kind
data_elements.description: Kind of account or evidence: witness statement, sensor reading, trace, product or document.

data_elements.name: reporter_ref
data_elements.description: Agent that reported the account (FHIR reportedReference; PROV attribution).

data_elements.name: reported_at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the account was reported.

data_elements.name: is_primary_source
data_elements.description: Whether the account is a primary source-of-truth record or a secondary report (PROV hadPrimarySource; FHIR reported[x]).

data_elements.name: reliability
data_elements.description: Reliability assigned to the reporting source.

data_elements.name: certainty
data_elements.description: Certainty of the occurrence claim, understood as a function of corroboration rather than a single stored flag.

data_elements.name: quoted_from_ref
data_elements.description: Entity the account was quoted from (PROV wasQuotedFrom).

artifacts.name: Source account
artifacts.description: An account or evidence record from which an occurrence was asserted, with reporter, time, primacy and reliability.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the reporter reference plus report time, and where available the primary source entity identifier.

layers.name: Record lifecycle
layers.description: Status of the happening and of the record, including scheduled-versus-occurred, amendment, error and invalidation.

findings.name: Status, amendment and invalidation
findings.description: Two status planes must not be collapsed. World-status for scheduled public events uses schema.org EventStatusType: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled, EventMovedOnline, with previousStartDate. Clinical/process status uses FHIR EventStatus: preparation, in-progress, not-done, suspended, aborted, completed, entered-in-error, unknown, with statusReason and the rule that not-done reason is only valid when status is not-done. Record-status uses PROV generation and invalidation (generatedAtTime, invalidatedAtTime, wasInvalidatedBy) plus EPCIS action ADD (commission), OBSERVE, DELETE (decommission). Amendment is a new revision (wasRevisionOf) or a qualified update, not a silent overwrite. Entered-in-error and not-done are record or process outcomes, not additional world happenings.

questions.text: What is the scheduled-event status, the process status, and the record status, and which plane is authoritative for this instance?
If the activity was not done, aborted, cancelled, postponed or entered in error, what statusReason applies and which previousStartDate values exist?
Was this record amended, and which prior revision, invalidating activity and timestamps apply?
Does this visibility event commission, observe or decommission the object identities it lists?

data_elements.name: world_or_schedule_status
data_elements.description: Schedule-plane status from schema.org EventStatusType such as EventScheduled, EventCancelled or EventPostponed.

data_elements.name: process_status
data_elements.description: Process-plane status from FHIR EventStatus such as preparation, in-progress, not-done, completed or entered-in-error.

data_elements.name: record_status
data_elements.description: Record-plane status covering generation and invalidation of the record that stands for the happening.

data_elements.name: status_reason
data_elements.description: Reason for the status, valid as a not-done reason only when the status is not-done.

data_elements.name: previous_start
data_elements.description: Previous start date of a postponed or rescheduled scheduled event.

data_elements.name: revision_of_ref
data_elements.description: Prior record revision that this record amends (PROV wasRevisionOf).

data_elements.name: invalidated_at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the record was invalidated (PROV invalidatedAtTime).

data_elements.name: epcis_action
data_elements.description: EPCIS action ADD (commission), OBSERVE or DELETE (decommission) applied to the listed object identities.

artifacts.name: Occurrence status history
artifacts.description: Versioned status of schedule, process and record planes with reasons, previous start times and invalidation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus status plane and revision, ordered by ingestion time.

bundles.name: Governance
bundles.description: Stewardship, disclosure, retention and alignment of occurrence records.
bundles.rationale: Stewardship, retention and interoperability are operating concerns over occurrence records, grouped so that disclosure, deletion and conformance rules stay together and cannot drift apart.

layers.name: Stewardship and access
layers.description: Who owns or maintains the record, who may see participation, and how exceptions are audited.

findings.name: Ownership, authority and disclosure
findings.description: Schema.org Event.owner and organizer are not automatically the record steward. The registry owner archetype is the primary actor, or the observing registrar when no actor records the happening. PROV wasAttributedTo / wasAssociatedWith record responsibility for the record entity versus the activity. FHIR relevantHistory points at Provenance of key transitions. CloudEvents privacy guidance: do not put sensitive information in inspectable context attributes; encrypt domain data; use protocol security. Participants control disclosure of their own participation; a public chronicle omits non-consenting participants rather than publishing redacted names as if complete.

questions.text: Who is the steward of this occurrence record, and is that party the primary actor, organizer, owner or observing registrar?
Under what authority was this account recorded, and which agent is attributed for the record versus associated with the activity?
Which participation facts are public, grant-restricted or omitted, and which grants authorize a personal timeline versus a public chronicle?
What lawful or safety exception overrides default non-disclosure, and how is that exception audited?

data_elements.name: steward_ref
data_elements.description: Party responsible for the occurrence record, which may be the primary actor or the observing registrar.

data_elements.name: owner_ref
data_elements.description: Owner of the event as recorded by schema.org Event.owner, which is not automatically the record steward.

data_elements.name: organizer_ref
data_elements.description: Organizer of the happening, distinct from steward and owner.

data_elements.name: disclosure_scope
data_elements.description: Whether participation facts are public, grant-restricted or omitted.

data_elements.name: participant_grant_refs
data_elements.description: Grants by which participants authorize disclosure of their own participation.

data_elements.name: public_chronicle_ok
data_elements.description: Whether the occurrence may appear in a public chronicle, with non-consenting participants omitted entirely.

artifacts.name: Stewardship and disclosure record
artifacts.description: Steward, owner, organizer and per-participant disclosure grants for an occurrence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus steward reference.

layers.name: Retention and deletion
layers.description: How long occurrence records and participation facts are kept, redacted or erased.

findings.name: Retention, redaction and erasure
findings.description: Occurrence identity and participation facts have different retention fates. FHIR entered-in-error and Provenance invalidation support tombstones rather than silent deletion of a happening that other records cite. CloudEvents advises linking to large or sensitive payloads rather than embedding them so access control can differ from event distribution. Participant erasure (personal-data rights) may redact participation while leaving a skeletal public occurrence, or may suppress the occurrence from a personal timeline. Legal hold freezes deletion. There is no single global retention period; sector and jurisdiction rules apply.

questions.text: What retention class applies to the occurrence record versus participation facts, and until when is each retained?
Is the record under legal hold, and which authority forbids deletion or amendment?
If a participant requests erasure, is participation redacted, the personal timeline suppressed, or a tombstone left for citers?

data_elements.name: retention_class
data_elements.description: Retention class applied to the occurrence record, with participation facts scheduled separately.

data_elements.name: retain_until
data_elements.description: Instant until which the record is retained under its retention class.

data_elements.name: legal_hold
data_elements.description: Whether a legal hold freezes deletion or amendment of the record.

data_elements.name: redaction_status
data_elements.description: Whether participation facts have been redacted or suppressed following a grant withdrawal or erasure request.

data_elements.name: erasure_request_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the erasure or grant-withdrawal request that authorized redaction.

data_elements.name: tombstone
data_elements.description: Whether a tombstone remains for citers instead of physical deletion.

artifacts.name: Occurrence retention schedule
artifacts.description: Retention class, hold, redaction and erasure state for an occurrence record and its participation facts.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus retention class, with participation facts scheduled separately.

layers.name: Interoperability
layers.description: Alignments, conflicts and the bootstrap contract for agents operating the model.

findings.name: Alignment profile and known conflicts
findings.description: External standards are alignments. CIDOC E5 is a change-bearing process; schema.org Event is often a cancellable scheduled public happening; FHIR Event is an activity that has occurred or is ongoing, usually with a subject; CloudEvents Event is a data record of a software occurrence; EPCIS events are visibility observations of identified objects; BFO models unfolding occurrents as processes, not a separate Event class; PROV Activity always acts on entities. Mapping tables must record these conflicts and must not claim conformance without evidence. Recurring schedules, locations, persons, acts, encounters, situations, audit trails and access grants are sibling models.

questions.text: Which external event classes is this occurrence aligned to, and is conformance actually claimed with evidence?
Which known conflicts apply (scheduled-versus-occurred, required subject, agentive-only, envelope-versus-occurrence, process-versus-event)?
Which sibling models (act, encounter, location, person, organization, situation, phenomenon, schedule, audit, access grant, supply-chain trace) are referenced rather than duplicated?

data_elements.name: alignment_targets
data_elements.description: External event classes to which this occurrence is aligned.

data_elements.name: conformance_claimed
data_elements.description: Whether conformance to an aligned standard is actually claimed, which requires per-instance evidence.

data_elements.name: conflict_flags
data_elements.description: Known conflicts carried with the mapping, such as scheduled-versus-occurred, required subject, agentive-only, envelope-versus-occurrence and process-versus-event.

data_elements.name: mapping_artifact_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the alignment map artifact holding the per-record mapping.

artifacts.name: Occurrence alignment map
artifacts.description: Per-record mapping to CIDOC, schema.org, PROV, EPCIS, CloudEvents, FHIR and BFO with conflict flags.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence or model identifier plus alignment target vocabulary.

artifacts.name: AGENTS.md bootstrap
artifacts.description: Mandatory agent bootstrap contract naming the model, type, specification, storage type, interface and processes URLs.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Fixed filename AGENTS.md at the model package root, resolved ahead of the Specification URL.

functions.name: Record occurrence
functions.description: Create an occurrence record from a source account, assigning master identity, dual timestamps, optional place and participation, without requiring an agent.
inputs: master-system identifier or recorded absence of one
outputs: occurrence record with master identity and dual timestamps
preconditions: A source account and steward are supplied
A master-system identifier exists, or its absence is recorded before a Dimension UUID or ULID is generated
No date or calendar label is used as the identifier
effects: A new occurrence record is created
Event time and observation or ingestion time are stored separately whenever they differ
Agentless happenings are accepted without a performer or subject

functions.name: Amend occurrence
functions.description: Correct recorded facts by creating a revision linked with wasRevisionOf or qualified invalidation, preserving prior versions for provenance.
outputs: new revision linked to the prior record
effects: Prior versions are preserved for provenance
A revision link or qualified invalidation is recorded
Identity, event time and the original source account are never silently overwritten

functions.name: Corroborate occurrence
functions.description: Attach an independent source account and recompute certainty; do not silently overwrite the first account.
outputs: attached source account and recomputed certainty
preconditions: The added account is independent of the accounts already held
effects: Certainty is recomputed from corroboration rather than set as a single flag
The first account is retained unchanged

functions.name: Dispute occurrence
functions.description: Record a formal contest of the account, holding competing source records without collapsing them into one certainty flag.
outputs: dispute record holding competing source accounts
preconditions: The disputed occurrence record and the contested account are identified
effects: Competing accounts are held side by side
Accounts are not collapsed into a single certainty flag

functions.name: Assert influence link
functions.description: Assert a qualified cause, contribution, communication, derivation or continuation between occurrences or entities, with asserter and confidence.
preconditions: Both ends of the link are identified
The claim is not derived solely from temporal overlap or co-location
effects: A directed qualified influence link is appended with asserter, time and confidence

functions.name: Compose episode
functions.description: Group member occurrences into a composite episode or super-event, or record fulfillment of a request or physical aggregation.
inputs: optional parent and child object identifiers
preconditions: Instance start and end are not asserted when a Schedule owns those dates
effects: Membership and parent links are recorded
Derived episode span and member count are recomputed
Fulfillment of a request or a physical aggregation action is recorded

functions.name: Project timeline
functions.description: Produce a personal timeline, public chronicle or causal graph projection that omits non-consenting participation.
inputs: projection kind (personal timeline, public chronicle or causal graph)
query filters over time, place, participant, type or episode
preconditions: Caller grants are resolved before any participation is included
effects: Non-consenting participation is omitted rather than published as if complete
Sensitive facts are kept out of inspectable context attributes

functions.name: Redact participation
functions.description: Remove or suppress a participant's involvement under grant withdrawal or erasure while retaining a tombstone or skeletal occurrence as required by citers.
outputs: redacted participation facts with retained tombstone or skeletal occurrence
preconditions: An erasure or grant-withdrawal artifact exists
effects: Participation is suppressed or removed
A tombstone or skeletal occurrence remains for citers
Personal-timeline projections may be suppressed

functions.name: Invalidate or mark entered-in-error
functions.description: End the usable life of an occurrence record via PROV invalidation or FHIR entered-in-error, recording the invalidating activity and time.
outputs: invalidated or entered-in-error record with tombstone
preconditions: The invalidating activity and time are known
effects: The usable life of the record ends
Invalidation is recorded instead of physical deletion
Citers still resolve a tombstone

functions.name: Interchange event
functions.description: Map an occurrence to or from CIDOC E5, schema.org Event, EPCIS, CloudEvents, PROV Activity or FHIR Event without implying conformance not evidenced by the alignment map.
inputs: occurrence record or external event payload
outputs: mapped event representation with conflict flags
preconditions: An alignment map exists for the target vocabulary
Conformance is claimed only where evidenced
effects: The occurrence is mapped to or from the external event class
Conflict flags are carried with the mapping
Envelope attributes remain distinct from the world occurrence

composition.purpose: Act specializes an occurrence by adding an intentional or causal actor (CIDOC E7 Activity carried out by an Agent; PROV Activity associated with an Agent).
Encounter specializes an occurrence by adding reciprocal participation; FHIR Encounter is an Event-pattern resource and must not replace the generic happening.
A supply-chain trace composes custody and visibility occurrences (EPCIS ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent, AssociationEvent).
Align to CIDOC E5 Event and, when agentive, E7 Activity; use P4, P7, P11, P12, P9 meronymy and P15 influence. Not a claim of CRM conformance.
Align public chronicle projections to schema.org Event, EventStatusType, subEvent/superEvent and attendance mode. Scheduled cancellable events remain a plan until they occur.
Compose OWL-Time Instant, Interval, duration, TRS and Allen relations as the temporal value types of an occurrence.
Align agentive occurrences to PROV Activity with used, wasGeneratedBy, wasAssociatedWith, wasInformedBy and qualified roles. Non-agentive happenings have no required Agent.
Align object-visibility occurrences to EPCIS event types and the what/when/where/why dimensions, including eventTime versus recordTime.
Align the event record envelope to CloudEvents id, source, type, subject and time. CloudEvents Event is the data record, not the world occurrence.
Align clinical process happenings to the FHIR Event pattern (status, occurrence versus recorded, performer, partOf, basedOn). Do not impose Event.subject 1..1 on generic world events.

Align unfolding happenings to BFO Process (occurrent with temporal proper parts and participants). Instantaneous beginnings and endings align to process boundaries, not a BFO Event class, which does not exist.
Place specifications resolve to addresses, geocodes, features and POIs mastered elsewhere; this model stores granularity and attendance mode.
Human participants are references to a person model.
Organizational participants, organizers and stewards are references to an organization model.
Recurring patterns or kinds are instantiated by particular occurrences recorded here.
Occurrences open, advance and close situations; standing conditions are not occurrences.
Record-keeping actions over occurrences are audited in an audit-trail sibling; FHIR relevantHistory is the clinical analogue.
Repeating schedules, plans and requests are not occurrences; instances that happen are. Schema.org eventSchedule forbids startDate/endDate on the Event when a Schedule is used.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension owns the occurrence kind scheme registry, because this model supplies no normative global event typology.
The adopting Dimension declares its temporal reference system and calendar defaults, and records the absence of a master-system identifier before generating a Dimension UUID or ULID.
The adopting Dimension publishes AGENTS.md naming the model, type, specification, storage type, interface and processes URLs, independent of the storage or interface projection in use.
The adopting Dimension maintains the alignment map and conflict flags for every external event vocabulary it claims.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Identifiers are namespaced by the producing source: a CloudEvents source plus id pair must be unique per event record, kind codes carry their scheme URI, and role codes carry their role scheme URI. Reverse-DNS type names are routing classes and must not be reused as occurrence identifiers, and dates or calendar labels are never namespace keys.
registry_links: CIDOC CRM entity and property registry (SRC-001, SRC-002) for E5/E7, E52 Time-Span and P-property alignment.
schema.org Event and EventStatusType vocabularies (SRC-003, SRC-004) for public-chronicle projections and schedule-plane status.
GS1 CBV business step and disposition vocabularies (SRC-008) for visibility events, which are GS1-centric and must be replaced per industry.

canonicalization_rules: Instant timestamps are canonicalized to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; unknown local offset uses -00:00.

Identity is canonicalized in priority order: authoritative master-system identifier, then governed global identifier or IRI, then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; dates and appellations are never canonical keys.
Kind, role, status and disposition values are canonicalized as code plus scheme URI, never as bare labels.
Non-Gregorian temporal positions are canonicalized against a declared TRS with an explicit precision unit and an ordering rule.
patch_rules: Amendments create a revision linked with wasRevisionOf or a qualified invalidation; identity, event time and the original source account are never silently overwritten.
Source accounts and influence links are append-only knowledge claims; corroboration adds an account instead of editing the first.
Status changes are patched with statusReason and, where a schedule is in play, previousStartDate; a not-done reason is only valid when the status is not-done.
Participation redaction is applied through an erasure or grant-withdrawal artifact and leaves a tombstone for citers.
compatibility_rules: External vocabularies are alignments: adding or changing an alignment updates the alignment map and conflict flags and never asserts conformance without evidence.
Profiles may tighten cardinality, for example by requiring a subject or performer, but the generic occurrence must remain valid with no agent at all.
Storage and interchange projections (JSON, YAML, HTML, Git, MCP, MongoDB, CloudEvents envelopes) may change without changing occurrence semantics.

identity_priority: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Record event time (when the occurrence happened) separately from observation or ingestion time (when a source captured or a registrar ingested the record) whenever those instants differ. Unqualified local time is not permitted; unknown offset may use -00:00. Non-Gregorian TRS values are additional, not a replacement for the RFC 3339 rule on instant timestamps.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Occurrence records are not serially numbered. Where a Dimension issues serials for revisions or status-history entries, the serial is scoped to the parent occurrence identifier and ordered by ingestion time, and never replaces the master-system identifier or serves as the occurrence primary key.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Occurrence identity is stable; amendments create revisions with provenance rather than silent overwrite. Causal links and source accounts are append-only knowledge claims. Invalidation and entered-in-error leave tombstones for citers. Participation redaction must not rewrite history as if the party had never been recorded without an erasure artifact.

policies: Distinguish the world occurrence from the event record; never treat a cancellable scheduled EventStatus as proof that a happening occurred.
Do not require an agent, subject or performer on the generic occurrence; those constraints belong to Act, Encounter or a FHIR Event profile.
Least disclosure of participation: public chronicles omit non-consenting parties rather than emitting incomplete participant lists as complete.
External standards are alignments; store conflict flags and forbid conformance claims without an evidenced mapping.
Dual timestamps are mandatory when event time and observation or ingestion time differ; CloudEvents producer fallback must be labelled as time_basis, not as event_time.
Sensitive participation and payload facts must not be copied into inspectable interchange context attributes.

read: Return occurrence core, time, place and public type according to the caller's grant.
Omit or anonymize participation the caller is not authorized to see.
Support time-range, place, participant, type, causal-neighbour and episode queries.
Expose alignment maps and conflict flags with the record.
create: Require a source account, steward, ingestion time and master-system identifier, or a generated Dimension UUID only after master-system absence is recorded.
Capture event time when known, with RFC 3339 seconds and offset or Z.
update: Amend via revision linked to the prior record; never silently overwrite identity, event time or original source.
Allow certainty to rise only by adding independent accounts.
Allow status-plane changes with statusReason and previousStartDate where a schedule is in play.
Recompute derived duration and episode span after member changes.
delete: Prefer invalidation, entered-in-error or participation redaction over physical delete.
On erasure requests, redact participation and optionally suppress personal-timeline projections while leaving citers a tombstone.
Physical deletion of an unused draft record is allowed only when no external identifier was published.

roles.name: Primary actor
responsibilities: May record the happening they carried out.
Controls disclosure of their own participation.
May dispute an account that misstates their role.

roles.name: Observing registrar
responsibilities: Records happenings with no actor or when actors do not file.
Maintains dual timestamps and source accounts.

roles.name: Participant
responsibilities: May grant or withdraw disclosure of their involvement.
May request redaction or erasure of participation facts.

roles.name: Steward
responsibilities: Owns quality, retention and alignment of the record.

roles.name: Corroborating source
responsibilities: Does not overwrite the first account.

roles.name: Auditor
responsibilities: Reads provenance, grants, invalidations and access exceptions.
Cannot alter occurrence facts except via logged review findings.

access.default_rule: Deny participation detail and sensitive payload; allow existence, type and public time/place of an occurrence only when the steward has marked it public or a grant applies. Agentless public chronicles remain visible; non-consenting participants are omitted entirely.
exceptions: Lawful compelled disclosure or safety exception, logged with legal basis and auditor identity.
Steward and registrar read of full participation for record-keeping.
Participant read of their own involvement even when the public chronicle omits them.
audit_requirements: Log create, amend, corroborate, dispute, grant change, redaction, invalidation and interchange mapping with actor, artifact identifier, event time and ingestion time.
Retain access-exception logs for at least as long as the occurrence record they refer to.

read_order: storage-type description at Storage type URL
process and function descriptions at Processes URL

coverage.claim: Wide-union operating surface for a generic occurrence: identity, kind, time including fuzzy and non-Gregorian TRS, place and attendance, participation and roles, influence and meronymy, source certainty, dual timestamps, record lifecycle, stewardship, access, retention and alignments to CIDOC CRM E5, schema.org Event, OWL-Time, PROV-O, EPCIS, CloudEvents, FHIR Event and BFO Process. Not a claim of universal ontology or of conformance to those standards.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier, governed IRI, then Dimension UUID/ULID; CloudEvents source+id uniqueness; CIDOC P1/P48; dates forbidden as identifiers.
Separate schedule status (EventStatusType), process status (FHIR EventStatus) and record status (PROV generation/invalidation, EPCIS action).
Participation, presence, used/generated entities, influence, meronymy, series, basedOn fulfillment and sibling-model references.
OWL-Time instants/intervals, CIDOC E52 inner/outer bounds, RFC 3339 instants with seconds and offset, dual event versus observation/ingestion time, TRS and Allen order.
Source accounts, primary source, attribution, quotation, revision, reporter versus registrar.
Steward versus owner versus organizer versus observing registrar; PROV attribution versus association.
Constraints: no date-as-id; dual timestamps when they differ; not-done reason only with not-done; schedule-owned dates; overlap is not causation; subject not required.
Default deny on participation; grants; public chronicle omission; CloudEvents cleartext-context warning; access exceptions audited.
Retention class, legal hold, participation redaction, tombstones, entered-in-error; no universal retention period.
ALIGN/COMPOSE/REFERENCE/EXTEND maps with explicit conflicts; AGENTS.md bootstrap independent of MongoDB or MCP storage.
Place specification, granularity, relative frames, virtual attendance, EPCIS readPoint versus bizLocation.
Independent accounts, corroboration, contradiction, qualified influence confidence.
Boundary with plan/schedule sibling; cancelled or postponed schema.org events are not world occurrences.

known_omissions: No normative global event typology; kind schemes are adopted per Dimension.
Relativistic spacetime beyond CIDOC E92/E93 Presence is not operationalized; marked as rare cultural-heritage alignment rather than a required layer.
RFC 5545 iCalendar RECURRENCE-ID and exception dates were not fetched as a primary source in this pass; recurring calendars are bounded to schema.org Schedule and a schedule sibling.
Legal 'event of default' and insurance loss-event statutes are jurisdiction-specific and not modelled as core kinds.
Natural-language event extraction quality metrics are out of scope.
Counterfactual and possible-world happenings have no primary-standard representation here.
Quantum measurement events and sub-second distributed-systems happened-before calculi beyond PROV wasInformedBy are gaps.
Detailed geospatial CRS and moving-object trajectories belong in location and mobility siblings.
conflicts: schema.org Event is commonly a cancellable scheduled public happening; CIDOC E5 Event is a change-bearing process that occurred; they are not the same class.
BFO has Process and process boundary, not Event; calling a BFO process an event is a vernacular alignment only.
FHIR Event.subject is 1..1; generic world events may have no subject.
CloudEvents time MAY be producer fallback rather than occurrence time; EPCIS eventTime is the occurrence time and recordTime is distinct.
RFC 3339 describes instants with UTC offset and does not cover intervals, fuzzy bounds or non-Gregorian TRS required by OWL-Time and CIDOC E52.
PROV Activity implies acting on entities; CIDOC E5 includes agentless happenings such as earthquakes.
schema.org VirtualLocation versus CIDOC E53 Place (physical extent): virtual attendance is a mode, not a Place.
EPCIS action DELETE means decommission of object identity in the visibility system, not erasure of the occurrence record.
regional_assumptions: Civil-time instants default to Gregorian calendar with RFC 3339 offset; historical, archaeological and geologic occurrences must declare a TRS.
Leap seconds are representable (second=60) but not predictable; applications must not invent future leap-second timestamps.
Privacy and erasure expectations assume a jurisdiction in which participation can be personal data; public-chronicle rules still omit non-consenting parties.
Daylight-saving and political timezone changes make unqualified local time non-interoperable, as RFC 3339 requires.
EPCIS CBV business steps are GS1-centric; other industries must supply their own bizStep schemes.
adversarial_checks: Would a cancelled concert be stored as an occurrence? No: it remains a scheduled Event/plan until a world happening occurs; EventCancelled is schedule-plane status only.
Would an earthquake be rejected for lack of performer or subject? No: agentless E5 Events are in scope.
Would two CloudEvents with the same source+id be treated as two happenings? No: they are duplicate records of one occurrence, possibly a retransmission.
Would overlapping intervals be ingested as causation? No: Allen overlap and co-location are temporal/spatial relations, not P15/PROV influence.

Would a participant-erasure request delete the Battle of Stalingrad record because one soldier is named? No: redaction of participation, not destruction of the public occurrence, unless the record is only that person's private timeline.
Would storing JSON in MongoDB or exposing MCP tools change the semantics? No: those are projections; AGENTS.md still names specification, storage type, interface and processes URLs.
